questions.question: Which act gave statutory status to the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)** was initially established in **1964**, following the recommendations of the **Santhanam Committee**, as an autonomous body to address corruption in government organizations.
 
• The **CVC Act, 2003** was enacted to grant **statutory status** to the Commission, ensuring its independence and enhancing its powers to combat corruption effectively.
 
• Under this Act, the CVC became a **statutory body**, meaning it has a legal foundation and its functioning is governed by laws specifically enacted for it. *Hence, the correct answer is The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.*
 
• **Key Provisions:** The CVC Act, 2003 outlines the composition, powers, and functions of the Commission. It defines its role in supervising vigilance activities in government departments and organizations.
 
• The Act also ensures the **independence** of the CVC by making it directly responsible to the President of India rather than subordinate to any ministry. *Hence, this Act was pivotal in strengthening anti-corruption measures in India.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overview of the Central Vigilance Commission:**

 
 
• **Establishment:** The CVC was created in **1964**, following recommendations by the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption.
 
• **Objective:** Its primary role is to monitor and supervise vigilance activities in various government departments to prevent corruption.
 
• **Statutory Status:** The enactment of the **CVC Act in 2003** gave it legal backing, ensuring its independence and authority.
 
 
 
• **Functions of CVC:**
 
 
• The CVC oversees the vigilance activities in **central government organizations** and ensures adherence to anti-corruption measures.
 
• **Supervision:** It monitors the investigations conducted by the Central Bureau of Investigation (**CBI**) in cases of corruption.
 
• It advises central government authorities on vigilance matters and recommends actions against corrupt practices.
 
 
 
• **Key Provisions of the CVC Act, 2003:**
 
 
• The Act ensures that the CVC is an **independent body**, free from the influence of any ministry or department.
 
• It specifies that the CVC shall consist of a **Central Vigilance Commissioner** and not more than two **Vigilance Commissioners**.
 
• The Act grants the CVC the authority to **investigate complaints** against government officials and recommend appropriate action.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Relevant Acts and Bodies:**

 
 
• The **Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988** complements the CVC's efforts by providing a legal framework for prosecuting corruption cases.
 
• **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013:** This Act established the Lokpal to address corruption cases involving high-level public officials.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Acts:**
 
 
• **The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 1964:** This Act established the CVC but did not provide statutory status.
 
• **The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003:** This Act granted statutory status, enhancing the CVC's independence and effectiveness.
 
• **Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988:** Focuses on prosecuting corruption cases but does not establish an oversight body.
 
• **Lokpal Act, 2013:** While addressing corruption, its scope is different as it targets high-level officials, unlike the CVC's broader vigilance role.

questions.question: The Earth completes one rotation on its axis approximately in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24 hours**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rotation of the Earth:** The Earth completes one full rotation around its axis in approximately **24 hours**. This rotation is responsible for the alternation of day and night.
 
• The Earth's axis is tilted at an angle of approximately **23.5 degrees**, which plays a significant role in the variation of day length across seasons.
 
• The rotation occurs from **west to east**, which is why the Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• **Time Division:** The 24-hour rotation period is divided into **daytime** and **nighttime**. Daytime occurs when a part of the Earth faces the Sun, while nighttime occurs when it faces away from the Sun.
 
• This rotation impacts various Earth processes, including the **movement of air masses**, the creation of ocean currents, and the Coriolis effect. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **365 days:** This value refers to the Earth's **revolution around the Sun**, not its rotation on its axis.
 
• **30 days:** This corresponds roughly to a month and is unrelated to Earth's rotation.
 
• **12 hours:** This is the approximate time for half of a rotation (day or night), not the full rotation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rotation of Earth:**

 
 
• The Earth rotates around its axis, an imaginary line passing through the North and South Poles.
 
• The speed of rotation at the equator is approximately **1670 km/hour** or **465 meters/second**.
 
• The rotation is responsible for the apparent motion of celestial bodies like the Sun, Moon, and stars.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Earth's Rotation:**
 
 
• The rotation causes the **Coriolis effect**, influencing wind patterns and ocean currents.
 
• It leads to the formation of **time zones** across the globe based on the rotation and division of Earth into 24 zones.
 
• The rotation also affects the Earth's shape, making it an **oblate spheroid**, slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Revolution vs. Rotation:**
 
 
• **Revolution:** The Earth's movement around the Sun, taking approximately **365.25 days** and resulting in the change of seasons.
 
• **Rotation:** The spinning of Earth on its axis, taking approximately **24 hours** and causing day and night.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Effects of Earth's Rotation:**

 
 
• The alternation of day and night is one of the most visible effects of Earth's rotation.
 
• The rotation influences the direction of wind systems and ocean currents due to the **Coriolis effect**.
 
• It also impacts the biological rhythms of living organisms, including humans, known as **circadian rhythms**.
 
 
 
• **Interesting Facts:**
 
 
• The Earth's rotation is gradually slowing down due to tidal forces, increasing the length of a day by approximately **1.7 milliseconds** every century.
 
• The phenomenon of **precession** causes a slow change in the orientation of Earth's axis over a period of **26,000 years**.

questions.question: Which British Prime Minister officially announced the decision to grant independence to India and withdraw British forces from the subcontinent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clement Atlee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Clement Atlee**, the **Prime Minister of the United Kingdom** from **1945 to 1951**, officially announced the decision to grant independence to India in **February 1947**.
 
• This decision marked a significant turning point in history, as the British Empire had ruled India for nearly **200 years**.
 
• The announcement was made in the context of mounting **Indian nationalist movements**, including the efforts of leaders such as **Mahatma Gandhi** and **Jawaharlal Nehru**, and the **INA activities** led by **Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose**. Hence, statement is correct.
 
• Atlee declared the British intention to **withdraw from India** by June 1948. This decision was influenced by several factors such as the **economic strains** caused by World War II, growing pressure from **Indian independence movements**, and increasing difficulties in administering the colony.
 
• The process of independence was expedited by the appointment of **Lord Mountbatten** as the last Viceroy of India. Mountbatten worked to ensure a smooth transition, leading to the partition of India into **India and Pakistan** on **15th August 1947**. Hence, statement is correct.
 
• Atlee’s government also considered the ongoing communal violence between Hindus and Muslims, which led to the decision to partition the subcontinent. This was done to avoid further bloodshed and facilitate a manageable governance structure. Hence, statement is correct.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Clement Atlee.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Leading to India's Independence:**

 
 
• The **Second World War** (1939-1945) left Britain economically weakened, making it challenging to sustain its colonial rule in India.
 
• The rise of **Indian nationalist movements**, particularly the **Quit India Movement** of 1942, demonstrated the demand for complete independence and made colonial administration increasingly difficult.
 
• The **Royal Indian Navy Mutiny** (1946) and unrest in armed forces also showed Britain the declining control over its colonial subjects.
 
 
 
• **Role of Clement Atlee:**
 
 
• **Clement Atlee** was the first British Prime Minister to acknowledge that the colonial rule in India was no longer sustainable.
 
• He appointed **Lord Mountbatten** as Viceroy in 1947 to oversee the transition to independence and ensure that the process was completed peacefully.
 
• Atlee’s Labour government was ideologically inclined towards **decolonization**, which aligned with its domestic focus on social reforms and economic recovery.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India:**
 
 
• The communal tensions between Hindus and Muslims led to the decision to partition India into two nations – **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• The partition resulted in large-scale migration and violence, with millions displaced and thousands killed.
 
• The partition was enacted under the **Indian Independence Act, 1947**, which was passed by the British Parliament.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Contributions of Clement Atlee:**

 
 
• He played an instrumental role in ending colonial rule in India, marking the beginning of decolonization across the world.
 
• His government’s policies focused on ensuring a peaceful transition while addressing communal tensions in the subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Figures:**
 
 
• **Stafford Cripps:** Known for the **Cripps Mission** in 1942, which aimed to grant dominion status to India but failed due to lack of support.
 
• **Pethick Lawrence:** As Secretary of State for India, he emphasized negotiations and was part of the **Cabinet Mission** in 1946.
 
• **Winston Churchill:** Churchill, a staunch imperialist, opposed granting independence to India during his tenure as Prime Minister before Atlee.

questions.question: What was the theme of the 10th Governing Council Meeting of NITI Aayog that was held on 24 May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Theme of the 10th Governing Council Meeting:** The theme of the meeting was "**Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047**," which translates to "Developed States for a Developed India by 2047."
 
• **Objective:** The central focus of the meeting was to align state efforts with the national vision of transforming India into a developed nation by **2047**, marking the 100th year of India’s independence.
 
• **Collaboration:** The meeting emphasized strengthening the partnership between the central and state governments to achieve the goal of holistic development across all states in India.
 
• **Key Areas of Discussion:** The council discussed critical areas such as sustainable economic growth, equitable development, and innovative solutions to address challenges faced by states.
 
• **State Empowerment:** The theme reflected the importance of empowering states to take proactive roles in governance, development planning, and execution to meet the aspirational goals of **2047**.
 
• **National Vision:** The idea of "Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat" underscored the belief that the progress of individual states is intrinsically linked to the overall development of the nation.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About NITI Aayog:**

 
 
• **NITI Aayog** stands for **National Institution for Transforming India.** It was established in **2015**, replacing the Planning Commission.
 
• It serves as the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India, providing strategic and technical advice to the central and state governments.
 
• NITI Aayog focuses on fostering cooperative federalism by involving states in the decision-making process.
 
 
 
• **Vision @2047:**
 
 
• The year **2047** marks the centenary of India's independence, and the government envisions transforming the country into a **developed nation.**
 
• This includes achieving goals like sustainable development, equitable resource distribution, technological innovation, and improved quality of life for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Role of States in Development:**
 
 
• States play a crucial role in implementing policies and schemes, as they are closer to the population and understand localized needs better.
 
• The theme emphasizes decentralization and empowering states to take charge of their development, in alignment with the national vision.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Governing Council Meetings:**

 
 
• The Governing Council of NITI Aayog is the primary platform for dialogue between the **central government** and **state governments**.
 
• These meetings aim to address developmental priorities and challenges faced by states, fostering a spirit of cooperative federalism.
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas of the 10th Meeting:**
 
 
• The meeting emphasized areas like **sustainable growth, social justice, innovation, and technology adoption** to achieve development goals.
 
• It also discussed strategies for better implementation of government schemes and policy frameworks at the state level.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes on Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) encourages entrepreneurs to set up CBG plants, produce and supply CBG to Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) for sale as automotive and industrial fuels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT)** scheme was launched by the Government of India in **October 2018**. It aims to promote the use of **Compressed Bio Gas (CBG)** as an alternative, renewable fuel.
 
• The scheme encourages **entrepreneurs** to set up CBG plants and produce fuel using agricultural residue, municipal solid waste, and other biodegradable waste. *Hence, the statement in the question is correct.*
 
• Under SATAT, **Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs)**, such as Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), are authorized to procure CBG produced by these plants.
 
• The scheme aims to achieve environmental sustainability by reducing dependence on fossil fuels and promoting cleaner fuel alternatives. It also aligns with India's commitment to reducing **carbon emissions** under the Paris Agreement.
 
• SATAT provides significant opportunities for rural entrepreneurship and employment, as setting up CBG plants involves local resources and manpower. *Hence, this is a key initiative for sustainable transportation.*
 
• CBG under SATAT can be used as an **automotive fuel**, industrial fuel, and for power generation. It can also serve as a replacement for conventional natural gas.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT):**

 
 
• Launched by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in **2018**, SATAT is a significant initiative to promote **bio-energy** and reduce India's reliance on fossil fuels.
 
• The scheme supports the establishment of **CBG plants** and their integration into the fuel ecosystem, thereby promoting waste management and energy efficiency.
 
• SATAT also contributes to achieving India's **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement** by reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 
 
• **Compressed Bio Gas (CBG):**
 
 
• **CBG** is produced through the anaerobic decomposition of organic waste such as agricultural residue, cattle dung, and municipal solid waste.
 
• It is a renewable, cleaner fuel that can replace **natural gas**, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), and coal in industrial applications.
 
• CBG is also used for automotive purposes, offering a greener alternative to conventional fuels like diesel and petrol.
 
 
 
• **Role of Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs):**
 
 
• OMCs such as IOCL, BPCL, and HPCL play a pivotal role in the SATAT initiative by procuring CBG from producers.
 
• They ensure the distribution and accessibility of CBG across the country, integrating it into the energy supply chain.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of SATAT:**

 
 
• The SATAT initiative aims to set up **5000 CBG plants** across India by **2023-24**, producing approximately **15 million tonnes** of CBG annually.
 
• It promotes the use of **compressed biogas** as a sustainable and affordable alternative to conventional fuels.
 
• The initiative supports **waste-to-energy** programs and contributes to effective waste management practices in rural and urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Schemes:**
 
 
• **Biogas Programme:** This scheme focuses on the production of biogas for cooking and lighting purposes, primarily aimed at rural areas.
 
• **Waste to Energy Programme:** This initiative promotes technologies to convert municipal waste into energy but does not specifically address CBG production for OMCs.
 
• **Cent Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) Scheme:** While it promotes CBG production, it is not as comprehensive as SATAT in supporting entrepreneurs and integrating CBG into the fuel market.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to the Lakshadweep group of islands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannur Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kannur Islands** belong to the **Lakshadweep group of islands**, which are a group of 36 small islands located in the **Arabian Sea**, off the southwestern coast of India.
 
• The Lakshadweep islands are the smallest Union Territory of India and are known for their **pristine beaches, coral reefs, and biodiversity.**
 
• The name Lakshadweep translates to "**one hundred thousand islands**" in Sanskrit, symbolizing the many small islands that form this region. *Hence, option 1 is correct.*
 
• Other islands mentioned in the options, such as **Kamorta Island** and **Chowra Island**, belong to the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, which are located in the Bay of Bengal and do not form part of the Lakshadweep group.
 
• **Milo Island** is not a recognized island in India and does not belong to any Indian island group. *Hence, options 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lakshadweep Islands:**

 
 
• **Location:** The Lakshadweep islands are located approximately 200–440 km off the southwestern coast of **Kerala** in the Arabian Sea.
 
• The island group consists of **36 islands**, but only **10 islands are inhabited**. The capital of Lakshadweep is **Kavaratti.**
 
• **Famous Islands:** Some of the well-known islands include **Agatti, Minicoy, Bangaram, and Kalpeni**. They are renowned for their **coral reefs** and **marine biodiversity.**
 
• **Tourism:** Lakshadweep is a popular tourist destination, especially for its **water sports, diving, and snorkeling activities.**
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:**
 
 
• **Location:** These islands are located in the **Bay of Bengal** and consist of two major groups: the Andaman Islands and the Nicobar Islands.
 
• **Kamorta and Chowra Islands:** Kamorta Island and Chowra Island are part of the Nicobar group of islands and are not related to the Lakshadweep group.
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are known for their tropical forests, rich marine life, and historical significance.
 
 
 
• **Milo Island:**
 
 
• Milo Island is not a recognized or official island in India. It is not part of the Lakshadweep or Andaman and Nicobar groups.
 
• This option might be fictitious or incorrectly mentioned in the question.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Union Territories in India:**

 
 
• India has **8 Union Territories**, including **Lakshadweep, Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, and Ladakh.**
 
• The Union Territories are directly governed by the **Central Government**, unlike states which have their own governments.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance:**
 
 
• **Lakshadweep Islands:** These islands are known for their **coral reefs and lagoons**, making them ecologically important.
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:** These islands serve as an important naval base due to their strategic location in the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following British officials found India as an uncivilised country and had to be civilised, following which the English Education Act of 1835 was introduced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thomas Macaulay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thomas Macaulay** was a British historian and politician who played a key role in introducing English education in India. He viewed India as a culturally inferior and "uncivilised" country and believed that the British had a moral obligation to "civilise" Indians.
 
• Macaulay authored the famous **Macaulay's Minute on Education (1835)**, which advocated for the promotion of English education in India instead of traditional Indian education systems based on Sanskrit and Persian. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The English Education Act of **1835** was introduced following Macaulay's recommendations. This act shifted the focus of education in India to English as the medium of instruction and encouraged Western knowledge and literature. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Macaulay's ideas **were based on the belief that the British education system was superior and could help "enlighten" Indian society. He argued that English education would create a class of Indians who were "Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, opinions, morals, and intellect."
 
• While his policies were criticised for undermining traditional Indian knowledge systems and languages, they laid the foundation for Western-style education in India. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Thomas Macaulay.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of the English Education Act, 1835:**

 
 
• The act marked a shift from promoting traditional Indian education systems to focusing on English as the medium of instruction.
 
• It aimed to create a class of Indians educated in Western knowledge and values, who could assist in the administration and governance of the colony.
 
• Funding was diverted to institutions promoting Western education rather than traditional Indian schools.
 
 
 
• **Thomas Macaulay’s Role:**
 
 
• Macaulay served as a member of the **Supreme Council of India** from **1834 to 1838**. During this time, he wrote his famous Minute on Education.
 
• He believed that Western knowledge, particularly English literature and science, was far superior to Indian knowledge systems and advocated for prioritising it in the education system.
 
• Although his views were criticised for being elitist and dismissive of Indian traditions, they influenced the establishment of universities and schools that followed the British model.
 
 
 
• **Impact of English Education in India:**
 
 
• The introduction of English education led to the rise of an educated middle class in India, which played a crucial role in the independence movement.
 
• It also facilitated the spread of modern ideas, science, and technology, but led to the marginalisation of traditional Indian knowledge systems.
 
• Examples include institutions like **Calcutta University**, which became centres for higher learning and intellectual activities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Criticisms of Macaulay’s Policies:**

 
 
• Macaulay’s policies were criticised for dismissing Indian languages and traditional education systems, leading to cultural alienation among Indians.
 
• His emphasis on English education contributed to the socio-economic divide, as it primarily benefited the urban elite and excluded rural populations.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of English Education in India:**
 
 
• While Macaulay’s approach was controversial, it established the foundation for India’s modern education system and its global competitiveness in fields like information technology and science.
 
• English remains a dominant language in India, serving as a medium for national and international communication.

questions.question: Which of the following two rice varieties were unveiled as a part of India's genomeediting initiative in May 2025?

options.text: Pusa DST Rice 2 and Swarna Rice

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamala and Pusa DST Rice 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Genome editing initiative:** India launched a significant genome editing initiative to enhance agricultural productivity, focusing on creating new crop varieties with improved traits.
 
• **Kamala and Pusa DST Rice 1:** These two rice varieties were unveiled in **May 2025** as part of India’s genome editing initiative. Both varieties aim to improve resilience to environmental stress and increase productivity.
 
• **Pusa DST Rice 1:** This variety is developed using genome editing techniques to ensure enhanced tolerance to drought conditions, making it suitable for regions with limited water availability. It is highly beneficial for farmers facing unpredictable climate patterns.
 
• **Kamala Rice:** Named after a native Indian term, Kamala Rice is engineered to provide increased resistance to diseases and pests, ensuring higher yields and reduced dependency on chemical pesticides.
 
• **Importance:** The development of these rice varieties aligns with India’s efforts to ensure **food security**, address **climate change challenges**, and promote sustainable agriculture.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 330**__.

__
 
• **Article 330** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• This provision ensures adequate representation of SCs and STs in the legislative process, addressing historical inequalities and promoting social justice.
 
• The reservation under **Article 330** is based on the proportion of the population of SCs and STs in the country as determined by the **census**. Hence, this article provides a mechanism for equitable representation in the Lok Sabha.
 
• **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes** are groups recognized by the Constitution as socially and educationally disadvantaged, requiring special provisions to uplift them. This article contributes to reducing disparities. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Details of Reservation for SCs and STs in Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• **Article 330** ensures that seats are reserved for SCs and STs based on their population size, promoting their inclusion in the legislative process.
 
• The reservation is reviewed periodically based on **census data** to ensure accurate representation.
 
• This provision is part of India's effort to address **historical disadvantages and discrimination** faced by these communities.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 331:** Provides representation to the **Anglo-Indian community** in the Lok Sabha through nomination by the President. This is different from the reservation for SCs and STs.
 
• **Article 332:** Deals with the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the **Legislative Assemblies** of the states, not the Lok Sabha.
 
• **Article 334:** Specifies the **time duration** for the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies. Initially set for 10 years, this has been extended multiple times via constitutional amendments.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Article 330:**
 
 
• It ensures **political representation** for marginalized communities, enabling them to voice their concerns and participate in the decision-making process.
 
• The article upholds the principle of **equality** enshrined in the Constitution, fostering inclusivity in governance.

• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The reservation for SCs and STs was introduced to address their historical exclusion from governance and decision-making processes.
 
• The **Constitutional Assembly** recognized the need for such provisions to promote equality and social justice.
 
 
 
• **Extension of Reservation:**
 
 
• The reservation under **Article 330** was initially meant for 10 years but has been extended through **constitutional amendments** to ensure continued representation.
 
• For instance, the **104th Amendment Act, 2020** extended the reservation for SCs and STs in Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies until **2030**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary objective of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM)?

• **Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM):** Launched by the **Government of India** in **2016**, the primary objective of this mission is to transform rural areas into economically, socially, and physically sustainable regions with the provision of urban-like facilities while retaining the essence of rural life.
 
• The mission focuses on developing **rural clusters** by providing essential infrastructure and services, such as roads, electricity, water supply, sanitation, digital connectivity, healthcare, education, and skill development facilities.
 
• SPMRM is aimed at reducing the migration of rural population to urban areas by creating sustainable and inclusive communities in rural regions. This strengthens rural economies. *Hence, the correct answer is "Development of rural clusters with urban-like facilities."*
 
• The mission targets clusters of villages with a population of 25,000 to 50,000 in plain areas and 5,000 to 15,000 in hilly, tribal, and desert areas to ensure equitable development across regions.
 
• SPMRM operates through two distinct categories of clusters: **Non-Tribal Clusters** and **Tribal Clusters**, catering to the specific needs of these regions.
 
• The mission is a comprehensive approach that integrates various schemes of the government to provide urban-like amenities in rural areas, boosting the rural population's overall quality of life.

Independent schemes like Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) focus exclusively on skill development.
 
• **Option 4: Ensuring 100 days of wage employment in rural areas** – This refers to the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (**MGNREGA**), which ensures employment opportunities in rural areas. However, it is not the primary focus of SPMRM.
 
 
 
• **Implementation of SPMRM:**
 
 
• The mission identifies clusters that have potential for growth and provides them with the necessary support to become "Rurban" clusters through integrated and participatory planning.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of structural unemployment?

options.text: A worker choosing not to work due to a lack of job opportunities
A worker being unable to find a job due to discrimination
A worker losing their job due to a recession
A worker being unable to find a job due to a lack of skills in a new and expanding industry

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4) A worker being unable to find a job due to a lack of skills in a new and expanding industry.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Structural unemployment** occurs when there is a mismatch between the skills that workers possess and the skills required by employers for available jobs in the economy.
 
• This type of unemployment arises due to **technological advancements**, changes in market demand, or the emergence of new industries that require specialized skills.
 
• For example, workers in industries such as agriculture or manufacturing might face structural unemployment if those industries decline and they lack the skills needed to transition to growing sectors like technology or healthcare. *Hence, option 4 is correct.*
 
• Option 1: "A worker choosing not to work due to a lack of job opportunities" refers to voluntary unemployment rather than structural unemployment. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• Option 2: "A worker being unable to find a job due to discrimination" refers to unemployment caused by social or systemic biases rather than structural unemployment. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• Option 3: "A worker losing their job due to a recession" is an example of cyclical unemployment, which occurs due to economic downturns or contractions. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Unemployment:**

 
 
• **Structural Unemployment:** This occurs when workers' skills do not match the requirements of the job market. It is common during periods of rapid technological change or industry shifts.
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment:** This is linked to economic cycles. During recessions, demand decreases, leading to job losses. Conversely, during economic booms, employment opportunities increase.
 
• **Frictional Unemployment:** This occurs when workers are temporarily between jobs, such as recent graduates looking for work or individuals transitioning to new jobs.
 
• **Seasonal Unemployment:** This type is caused by changes in demand for labor due to seasonal patterns, such as agricultural work or tourism-related jobs.
 
• **Voluntary Unemployment:** This occurs when workers opt not to work, often due to personal preferences or lack of suitable opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Causes of Structural Unemployment:**
 
 
• **Technological advancements:** Automation and artificial intelligence can replace traditional jobs requiring manual labor or repetitive tasks.
 
• **Globalization:** Jobs may move overseas, leaving domestic workers unemployed if they lack the skills or opportunities to compete globally.
 
• **Educational limitations:** Workers may not have access to training programs or higher education needed to adapt to evolving industries.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Structural Unemployment:**
 
 
• The decline of coal mining jobs due to the shift to renewable energy.
 
• The reduction of manufacturing jobs in developed countries as production shifts to countries with lower labor costs.
 
• The rise of jobs requiring digital skills, such as programming, while workers in traditional industries may struggle to adapt to these requirements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Addressing Structural Unemployment:**

 
 
• **Government policies:** Governments can support workers through retraining programs, skill development workshops, and educational initiatives.
 
• **Private sector involvement:** Companies can contribute by offering on-the-job training or partnering with educational institutions to ensure the availability of skilled workers.
 
• **Long-term solutions:** Investments in education, research, and development can help prevent future structural unemployment by preparing workers for upcoming industry demands.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Structural Unemployment:**
 
 
• It can lead to **economic inequality**, as certain groups of workers are disproportionately affected.
 
• It may result in a **decline in living standards** for those unable to find suitable employment.
 
• Countries with high levels of structural unemployment may experience slower economic growth due to underutilized labor potential.

• **Article 149** of the Constitution specifies the duties and powers of the CAG, which include auditing the accounts of the Union and State governments, public sector enterprises, and other entities funded by the government.

In this type of bond, one atom donates electrons, becoming a positively charged **cation**, while the other atom accepts electrons, becoming a negatively charged **anion**. The electrostatic attraction between these oppositely charged ions forms the bond.
 
• **NaCl (Sodium Chloride):** Sodium chloride is a classic example of a compound formed by ionic bonding. In NaCl, **sodium (Na)** donates one electron to achieve a stable electronic configuration, forming a positive ion (Na⁺). Meanwhile, **chlorine (Cl)** accepts the electron to complete its octet, forming a negative ion (Cl⁻). The electrostatic attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions results in the ionic bond.
 
• Compounds like **NaCl** typically have a crystalline structure due to the arrangement of ions in a lattice format. These compounds exhibit high melting and boiling points and conduct electricity in molten or aqueous states. *Hence, NaCl is correct.*
 
• **Other Options:**

• **CO₂:** Carbon dioxide is also a covalent compound formed by sharing electrons between carbon and oxygen atoms. *Hence, incorrect.*
 
• **NH₃:** Ammonia is another example of a covalent compound formed by sharing electrons between nitrogen and hydrogen atoms. *Hence, incorrect.*
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is NaCl.***

__

questions.question: Who is credited with the discovery of the nucleus through the gold foil experiment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ernest Rutherford**__.

__
 
• **Ernest Rutherford** is credited with the discovery of the **atomic nucleus** through the famous **gold foil experiment**, conducted in **1909**.
 
• In this experiment, Rutherford and his colleagues **Hans Geiger** and **Ernest Marsden** bombarded a thin gold foil with alpha particles to observe their scattering pattern.
 
• Most of the alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil, while some were deflected at small angles, and a few were deflected at large angles. This observation was unexpected and led to groundbreaking conclusions. *Hence, Ernest Rutherford is the correct answer.*
 
• The results of the experiment demonstrated that the atom is mostly empty space, with a small, dense, positively charged center called the **nucleus**. This finding overturned J.J. Thomson's "plum pudding model" of the atom.
 
• Rutherford's nuclear model of the atom proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus, which contains most of the atom's mass. *Hence, this experiment revolutionized atomic theory.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Born:** **August 30, 1871** in New Zealand.
 
• Rutherford is often referred to as the **"Father of Nuclear Physics"** for his contributions to the understanding of atomic structure.
 
• He received the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1908** for his work on the disintegration of elements and the chemistry of radioactive substances.
 
 
 
• **Gold Foil Experiment:**
 
 
• The experiment involved directing **alpha particles** at a thin sheet of gold foil and measuring their scattering using a fluorescent screen.
 
• Most particles passed through the foil, indicating that atoms are mostly empty space. However, large deflections showed the presence of a dense, positively charged nucleus.
 
• This experiment led to the development of the **Rutherford atomic model**, which replaced the earlier "plum pudding model" proposed by J.J. Thomson.
 
 
 
• **Key Contributions of Other Scientists:**
 
 
• **Bohr:** Improved upon Rutherford's model by introducing **electron energy levels** in 1913.
 
• **John Dalton:** Proposed the ** in the early 19th century, suggesting that matter consists of indivisible atoms.
 
• Lavoisier:** Known as the **"Father of Modern Chemistry"**, he identified and named **oxygen** and contributed to the law of conservation of mass.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of Rutherford's Discovery:**

 
 
• Rutherford's work laid the foundation for the **modern atomic model** and further research into subatomic particles.
 
• It paved the way for the discovery of **protons** and later the **neutron** by James Chadwick in **1932**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Atomic Theory:**
 
 
• Rutherford's contributions are crucial in fields like **nuclear physics, chemistry, and material science**.
 
• His findings are used in technologies like **nuclear reactors, particle accelerators, and medical imaging**.

questions.question: Which of the following chemical reactions does NOT represent a balanced equation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A chemical equation is considered **balanced** when the number of atoms for each element is equal on both sides of the equation, adhering to the **Law of Conservation of Mass**.
 
• Let's analyze the chemical reactions provided in the question:
 
• **Option 1:** 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂
 
 
• This equation is balanced because the number of Fe, H, and O atoms are the same on both sides of the equation.
 
• *Hence, Option 1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** 4Fe + 3H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 2H₂
 
 
• This equation is **not balanced**. On the left side, there are 4 Fe atoms, but only 3 Fe atoms are present on the right side within Fe₃O₄.
 
• Additionally, the number of H atoms is not consistent between the sides; there are 6 H atoms on the left but only 4 H atoms on the right.
 
• *Hence, Option 2 is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** Fe + H₂O → FeO + H₂
 
 
• This equation is balanced because there is 1 Fe atom, 2 H atoms, and 1 O atom on each side of the equation.
 
• *Hence, Option 3 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** 2Fe + 3H₂O → Fe₂O₃ + 3H₂
 
 
• This equation is balanced as there are 2 Fe atoms, 6 H atoms, and 3 O atoms on each side of the equation.
 
• *Hence, Option 4 is correct.*
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:**

 
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Mass** states that matter cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction, meaning the total mass of reactants must equal the total mass of products.
 
• In a balanced chemical equation, the number of atoms for each element is equal on both sides, ensuring that the equation adheres to this law.
 
 
 
• **Balancing Chemical Equations:**
 
 
• To balance a chemical equation, one must ensure that the count of atoms for every element is equal on both sides of the equation.
 
• Coefficients are used before chemical formulas to adjust the number of molecules or atoms in a reaction.
 
• Example: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl is balanced because there are 2 hydrogen atoms and 2 chlorine atoms on both sides.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Balanced Equations:**
 
 
• Balanced equations are essential for calculating the amounts of reactants and products in a reaction.
 
• They are used in stoichiometry to determine the quantity of products formed or reactants required.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of Balanced Equations:**

 
 
• The equation must represent the actual chemical reaction.
 
• The physical states of reactants and products are often mentioned (e.g., solid, liquid, gas, aqueous).
 
• It provides information about reactants and products in their simplest ratio.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Real Chemical Reactions:**
 
 
• Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
• Combustion of methane: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.question: Which of the following minerals is known as 'Brown Coal' in India?

The correct answer is __**Lignite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lignite**, often referred to as "Brown Coal," is a type of soft coal that is primarily used as a fuel for generating electricity and energy production.
 
• It is considered to be a low-grade coal due to its lower carbon content compared to other types of coal like bituminous or anthracite. However, it is abundant and widely used in India for power generation.
 
• India has significant reserves of **Lignite**, particularly in states like **Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Jammu & Kashmir**. The Neyveli Lignite Corporation in Tamil Nadu is one of the largest producers of lignite in the country.
 
• **Lignite** is characterized by its brownish color and relatively high moisture and volatile matter content. This makes it less efficient in terms of energy output compared to higher-grade coal types, but it is still a vital resource for thermal power plants. *Hence, lignite is called "Brown Coal" in India.*
 
• The term "Brown Coal" emphasizes the economic importance of lignite as a resource for energy production and industrial applications in India. *Hence, lignite is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lignite Characteristics:**

 
 
• **Lignite** is a sedimentary rock that is formed from compressed peat deposits over geological time.
 
• It typically has a **carbon content of 25–35%** and a high **moisture content (up to 66%).** This makes lignite a less efficient fuel compared to higher-grade coal types.
 
• The heating value of lignite ranges between **9–17 megajoules per kilogram**, which is lower than that of bituminous coal and anthracite.
 
 
 
• **Major Lignite Reserves in India:**
 
 
• India has abundant lignite reserves, with major deposits located in **Neyveli (Tamil Nadu), Barmer (Rajasthan), Gujarat, and Jammu & Kashmir.**
 
• The **Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC)** is one of the leading producers of lignite in India and is engaged in the mining and utilization of lignite for power generation.
 
• **Neyveli Lignite Mines** in Tamil Nadu are among the most significant lignite mines in India, contributing substantially to the energy sector.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Lignite:**
 
 
• Lignite is primarily used in **thermal power plants** to generate electricity.
 
• It is also used as a raw material in industries for the production of **synthetic natural gas, fertilizer, and other chemical products.**
 
• Some lignite deposits are utilized in the production of **activated carbon** and other industrial goods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Coal Types:**

 
 
• **Mica:** Mica is not a type of coal; it is a mineral used in the electrical and electronics industry due to its insulating properties.
 
• **Copper:** Copper is a metal, not a coal type, and is primarily used in electrical wiring, electronics, and construction.
 
• **Bauxite:** Bauxite is an ore of aluminum and is unrelated to coal. It is primarily used in the production of aluminum metal.
 
 
 
• **Lignite's Importance:**
 
 
• Lignite plays a critical role in meeting India's **energy demands**, especially in regions with limited access to other fossil fuels.
 
• Its abundance makes it a **cost-effective resource** for energy production, despite its lower efficiency compared to other coal types.

questions.question: During the Mughal period, the Ain-i-Dahsala system was introduced by _____.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ain-i-Dahsala system** was introduced by **Akbar**, one of the greatest Mughal emperors, as a part of his revenue administration reforms.
 
• The system was developed by **Raja Todar Mal**, the Finance Minister of Akbar, to ensure a fair and systematic collection of land revenue.
 
• Under this system, land revenue was calculated based on the average produce and prices of crops over the last **10 years**. This helped create consistency and fairness in taxation. *Hence, Akbar introduced the Ain-i-Dahsala system.*
 
• **The system divided land into categories:** Polaj (cultivated yearly), Parauti (left fallow for 1-2 years), Chachar (left fallow for 3-4 years), and Banjar (left fallow for over 5 years).
 
• The system was widely regarded for its fairness and accuracy in assessing the agricultural productivity and tax potential of land. *Hence, the implementation of this system was a hallmark of Akbar's reign.*
 
• The Ain-i-Dahsala system also promoted a sense of trust between the farmers and the Mughal administration, as it removed arbitrary taxation. *Hence, the correct answer is Akbar.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akbar's Revenue Administration:**

 
 
• **Raja Todar Mal** played a crucial role in developing Akbar’s revenue system and introduced systematic measures for land taxation.
 
• Akbar implemented the **Zabt system**, under which land was surveyed and measured to assess its productivity and establish revenue rates.
 
• The **Ain-i-Dahsala system** was an important part of the Zabt system, ensuring revenue was collected based on a fair average of crop production and prices.
 
 
 
• **Categories of Land under the Ain-i-Dahsala System:**
 
 
• **Polaj:** Land cultivated annually.
 
• **Parauti:** Land left fallow for 1-2 years.
 
• **Chachar:** Land left fallow for 3-4 years.
 
• **Banjar:** Land left fallow for over 5 years.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Ain-i-Dahsala System:**
 
 
• It introduced a fair and predictable system of taxation, reducing the burden on farmers and encouraging agricultural productivity.
 
• The system promoted a sense of stability and trust between the Mughal administration and the agrarian community.
 
• It became a model for future revenue systems in India and influenced administrative practices during British rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of Akbar’s Revenue System:**

 
 
• Akbar’s system relied on a detailed survey of land to ensure accurate assessment of taxes.
 
• **Standardization:** The system standardized revenue collection, removing regional variations and arbitrary practices.
 
 
 
• **Role of Raja Todar Mal:**
 
 
• He was a skilled administrator who introduced scientific methods for land measurement and revenue assessment.
 
• His innovations in revenue collection became a benchmark for future governance in India.

questions.question: Special Economic Zones (SEZs) were established to promote export-oriented industrialisation. What is a primary incentive offered to firms operating in SEZs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tax holidays and infrastructure support**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Special Economic Zones (SEZs):**

 
 
• SEZs are designated geographical regions within a country where business and trade laws differ from the rest of the nation to promote economic growth and exports.
 
• These zones aim to attract foreign investment, enhance industrialization, and boost export-oriented growth. They are significant contributors to a country’s economic development.
 
 
 
• **Primary Incentives Offered:**
 
 
• **Tax holidays:** Firms operating in SEZs often enjoy exemptions from corporate taxes for a specific period, encouraging businesses to invest and operate within these zones. *Hence, this is correct.*
 
• **Infrastructure support:** SEZs provide state-of-the-art infrastructure, including transportation, communication, power supply, and other utilities, ensuring optimal business operations. This helps companies reduce operational costs and enhances productivity. *Hence, this is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Higher import duties:** SEZs aim to reduce import duties to facilitate the import of raw materials and technology. Offering higher import duties contradicts the purpose of SEZs and is incorrect.
 
• **Strict labour laws:** SEZs often have more flexible labour laws to attract investments and streamline operations. Strict labour laws are not a feature of SEZs and are incorrect.
 
• **Ban on foreign investments:** SEZs are established to attract foreign direct investments (FDIs). A ban on foreign investments would defeat the purpose of SEZs, making this option incorrect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Special Economic Zones in India:**

 
 
• India introduced SEZs in **2005** with the enactment of the **Special Economic Zones Act**. The primary goal was to enhance exports, attract foreign investment, and create employment.
 
• Prominent SEZs in India include **Noida SEZ**, **SEEPZ (Mumbai)**, and **Chennai SEZ**.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples of SEZs:**
 
 
• China established SEZs like **Shenzhen** in the late 20th century, which played a significant role in transforming the country into a global manufacturing hub.
 
• Dubai's **Jebel Ali Free Zone (JAFZA)** is another successful example, contributing to the city’s position as a global trade and logistics hub.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of SEZs:**
 
 
• Duty-free imports for companies operating within the zone.
 
• Tax exemptions for a specific period to attract investments.
 
• Enhanced infrastructure and logistics support for seamless operations.
 
• Simplified laws and regulations, including relaxed labour laws and streamlined customs processes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Impact of SEZs:**

 
 
• SEZs contribute significantly to a country’s **GDP growth** by promoting export-oriented industries.
 
• They create job opportunities and improve the standard of living in surrounding areas.
 
• SEZs attract **foreign direct investment (FDI)**, facilitating technology transfer and enhancing the global competitiveness of domestic industries.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by SEZs:**
 
 
• Land acquisition and displacement issues often create social and political challenges.
 
• Infrastructure development requires significant financial investment and time.
 
• Compliance with environmental regulations and managing ecological concerns can be challenging for SEZs.

questions.question: Special provisions for certain states are covered under which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XXI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Special provisions for certain states** in India are outlined under **Part XXI** of the Constitution, titled "Temporary, Transitional, and Special Provisions."
 
• This part of the Constitution primarily addresses the **unique conditions of certain states** and regions, allowing them to have special privileges and provisions due to their distinctive social, cultural, or geographical conditions.
 
• **Article 370** (now abrogated) provided special status to **Jammu & Kashmir**, granting it autonomy in various areas except defense, foreign affairs, finance, and communications. *Hence, this was part of Part XXI.*
 
• **Article 371** and its sub-clauses (Article 371-A to 371-J) provide **special provisions for states** like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, etc., focusing on administrative, cultural, and economic development. *Hence, this is covered under Part XXI.*
 
• These provisions ensure that the **rights and interests of the residents** in these states are safeguarded, considering their unique circumstances. *Hence, Part XXI applies to special provisions for certain states.*
 
• Part XXI reflects the **diverse nature of India** and acknowledges the need for flexible governance in states with distinct characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Special Provisions under Part XXI:**

 
 
• **Article 370**: Provided temporary provisions for Jammu & Kashmir, granting it autonomy in certain legislative areas. This article was abrogated in **August 2019**.
 
• **Article 371**: Contains special provisions for states like Maharashtra and Gujarat to ensure equitable distribution of resources and development.
 
• **Article 371-A**: Ensures the protection of the **customary laws** and social practices of Nagaland, as well as the religious and land-related rights of its people.
 
• **Article 371-B**: Provides special representation for the tribal areas of Assam in its legislature.
 
• **Article 371-J**: Grants special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, ensuring reservation in employment and education.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Part XXI:**
 
 
• Part XXI is unique to the Indian Constitution as it addresses **temporary, transitional, and special provisions**.
 
• It reflects India’s commitment to addressing the **diverse needs of its states** and regions, ensuring their protection and development.
 
• The provisions have helped integrate culturally, geographically, and administratively distinct states into the Indian Union.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Examples of Special Provisions:**

 
 
• **Nagaland (Article 371-A)**: Protects the cultural and religious practices of the Naga people, including their land ownership rights.
 
• **Assam (Article 371-B)**: Ensures political representation for tribal areas.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh (Article 371-D)**: Focuses on equitable opportunities in education and employment.
 
• **Karnataka (Article 371-J)**: Provides reservations for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region to address socio-economic disparities.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• Special provisions are created or amended through **constitutional amendments** based on the needs of specific states.
 
• For example, **Article 371-J** was added through the **98th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2012**.

• The company was established in **1981** as a joint venture between the **Government of India** and **Suzuki Motor Corporation** of Japan.
 
• Under the **Government of India’s disinvestment policy**, the majority of the government’s stake in Maruti Udyog Limited was sold to Suzuki during the early **2000s**.
 
• The disinvestment process was initiated to **reduce government involvement** in non-strategic sectors, promote private sector efficiency, and generate revenue.
 
• This move marked a significant step in India’s economic liberalization and privatization efforts. **Maruti Udyog Limited** became a wholly owned subsidiary of **Suzuki Motor Corporation**.
 
• The privatization of Maruti Udyog Limited boosted its performance and allowed it to become the leading automobile manufacturer in India.
 
• Other entities mentioned in the options—like **ISRO**, **BSNL**, and **LIC**—are either government organizations or undertakings that were not privatized during the 2000s. *Hence, the correct answer is Maruti Udyog Limited.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Maruti Udyog Limited (Maruti Suzuki India Limited):**

• Maruti Suzuki is known for introducing affordable and fuel-efficient vehicles, such as the **Maruti 800**, which revolutionized the automobile market in India.

questions.question: Who among the following formed a Satyagraha Sabha on 24 February 1919 in Bombay to protest against the Rowlatt Bills?

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** formed the **Satyagraha Sabha** on **24 February 1919** in **Bombay** to protest against the **Rowlatt Bills**.
 
• The Rowlatt Bills were officially known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, which gave the British government sweeping powers to suppress political activities and detain people without trial. Gandhi strongly opposed this act.
 
• The Satyagraha Sabha was formed as a platform to organize nonviolent protests and mobilize public opinion against the draconian laws imposed under the Rowlatt Act. *Hence, Mahatma Gandhi’s formation of the Sabha is correct.*
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** called for nationwide protests, including ** (strikes) and nonviolent resistance, and the Sabha became a pivotal institution for promoting Satyagraha** as a form of peaceful protest.
 
• The movement initiated by Gandhi reflected his philosophy of truth and nonviolence and marked the beginning of a new phase in India’s freedom struggle. *Hence, the correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.*

• The Act faced widespread opposition across the country because it violated basic civil liberties and was seen as an extension of oppressive colonial policies.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi’s Philosophy of Satyagraha:**
 
 
• **Satyagraha**, meaning "truth-force," was a method of nonviolent resistance developed by Mahatma Gandhi. It emphasized peaceful protests, truth, and self-discipline as tools to achieve political and social goals.
 
• Gandhi used Satyagraha in various movements, such as the **Champaran Satyagraha**, **Kheda Satyagraha**, and later, during the **Salt March** and Quit India Movement.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Satyagraha Sabha:**

• The protests organized under the Sabha eventually led to widespread agitation, culminating in events like the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** in April 1919.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:** A key leader in India's freedom struggle and the first Deputy Prime Minister of India, Patel did not form the Satyagraha Sabha. Hence, this option is **incorrect**.

• The **Rowlatt Act** and subsequent protests highlighted the growing dissatisfaction with British colonial rule and became a precursor to larger movements like the **Non-Cooperation Movement** of 1920.

questions.question: The number of prime numbers lying between 476 and 491, both included, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

List the odd numbers in the given range, excluding those ending in 5: 477, 479, 481, 483, 487, 489, 491.

Eliminate multiples of 3 by checking the sum of digits: 477, 483, and 489 are eliminated.

Remaining numbers to check: 479, 481, 487, 491.

Check divisibility for 481: 481 = 13 × 37, so it is not prime.

The remaining numbers 479, 487, and 491 are not divisible by any prime up to √500 ≈ 22, hence they are prime.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers lie between 476 and 491 (both included).

**Concept Used:**

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself.

To check if a number N is prime, we only need to test divisibility by prime numbers up to √N.

**Calculation:**

⇒ The numbers between 476 and 491 are: 476, 477, 478, 479, 480, 481, 482, 483, 484, 485, 486, 487, 488, 489, 490, 491.

⇒ First, exclude all even numbers and numbers ending in 5, as they cannot be prime.

⇒ The potential prime numbers left are: 477, 479, 481, 483, 487, 489, 491.

⇒ Check 477: 4 + 7 + 7 = 18 (Divisible by 3) → Not prime.

⇒ Check 479: √479 ≈ 21.8. Prime numbers to check ≤ 21 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. It is not divisible by any of these → Prime.

⇒ Check 481: 481 ÷ 13 = 37. It is exactly divisible by 13 → Not prime.

⇒ Check 483: 4 + 8 + 3 = 15 (Divisible by 3) → Not prime.

⇒ Check 487: √487 ≈ 22. Not divisible by any prime number ≤ 19 → Prime.

⇒ Check 489: 4 + 8 + 9 = 21 (Divisible by 3) → Not prime.

⇒ Check 491: √491 ≈ 22.1. Not divisible by any prime number ≤ 19 → Prime.

⇒ The prime numbers between 476 and 491 are 479, 487, and 491.

⇒ Total count of prime numbers = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

How to Check for Primality

To check if a number N is prime, calculate the approximate square root of N. Divide N by all prime numbers less than or equal to √N. If none divide N exactly, it is guaranteed to be a prime number.

Divisibility Rule for 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 (or 9) if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 (or 9). This rule is incredibly useful for quickly eliminating large composite numbers during prime number checks.

Co-Prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime (or relatively prime) if they do not have any common prime factor other than 1. Their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is always 1.
</p

questions.question: A bus travelling at 75 km/hr completes a journey in 17 hours. What should be its speed to cover the same distance in 5 hours?

New Time (T₂) = 5 hours

Distance = Speed × Time

If Distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional (S ∝ 1 / T). Therefore, the ratio of speeds is the inverse of the ratio of times taken.

When traveling equal distances at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed is given by (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, it is |S₁ − S₂|.

Let the two consecutive even numbers be (x − 1) and (x + 1), where x is the odd number exactly between them.

Sum of their squares: (x − 1)² + (x + 1)² = 1684

⇒ 2(x² + 1) = 1684

⇒ x² + 1 = 842 ⇒ x² = 841 ⇒ x = 29

The numbers are 29 − 1 = 28 and 29 + 1 = 30. Their sum is 28 + 30 = 58.

**∴ The correct answer is 58.**

⇒ x² + x² + 4x + 4 = 1684

⇒ 2x² + 4x − 1680 = 0

⇒ x² + 2x − 840 = 0

⇒ x² + 30x − 28x − 840 = 0

⇒ x(x + 30) − 28(x + 30) = 0

⇒ (x − 28)(x + 30) = 0

⇒ x = 28 (ignoring the negative value −30 as x must be a natural number)

⇒ The second consecutive even number = 28 + 2 = 30

⇒ Sum of the numbers = 28 + 30 = 58

questions.question: M and N start a business. M invests ₹38,000 more than N invests for 2 months and N for 3 months. M's share is ₹461 more than that of N, out of a total profit of ₹6,915. Find the capital contributed by M.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit of M = (6915 + 461) ÷ 2 = ₹3688 and Profit of N = 6915 − 3688 = ₹3227.

Profit ratio (M : N) = 3688 : 3227 = 8 : 7.

Capital ratio = (Profit of M ÷ Time of M) : (Profit of N ÷ Time of N) = (8 ÷ 2) : (7 ÷ 3) = 12 : 7.

Difference in capital ratio = 12 − 7 = 5 units = ₹38,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹7,600.

Capital contributed by M = 12 units = 12 × 7600 = ₹91,200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹91,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total profit = ₹6,915

M's profit − N's profit = ₹461

Time period of M = 2 months, Time period of N = 3 months

M's capital is ₹38,000 more than N's capital.

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = (Capital of A × Time of A) : (Capital of B × Time of B)

 
 Partner M
 Time = 2 months
 Capital = x + 38000
 Profit = ₹3688

 
 Partner N
 Time = 3 months
 Capital = x
 Profit = ₹3227
 
 Capital × Time ∝ Profit

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let M's profit be Pₘ and N's profit be Pₙ.

⇒ Pₘ + Pₙ = 6915

⇒ Pₘ − Pₙ = 461

⇒ Adding both equations: 2Pₘ = 7376 ⇒ Pₘ = 3688

⇒ Pₙ = 6915 − 3688 = 3227

⇒ Ratio of their profits = 3688 : 3227

⇒ Dividing by their common factor (461): Profit ratio = 8 : 7

⇒ Let N's capital be x. Then M's capital will be (x + 38000).

⇒ [2 × (x + 38000)] ÷ (3 × x) = 8 ÷ 7

⇒ 14 × (x + 38000) = 24x

⇒ 14x + 532000 = 24x

⇒ 10x = 532000

⇒ x = 53200

⇒ M's capital = x + 38000 = 53200 + 38000 = 91200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹91,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple vs Compound Partnership

In simple partnership, capitals are invested for the same time period, so profit is distributed strictly in the ratio of their investments. In compound partnership, investments are made for different time periods, so profit ratio = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂).

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and usually receives a fixed salary or percentage of the profit before the remaining profit is distributed. A sleeping partner only invests capital and receives a share from the distributable profit based on their investment ratio.

Finding Capital from Profit and Time

If the profit ratio and time ratio of partners are given, the ratio of their invested capitals can be found by directly dividing the profit ratio by the time ratio: Capital Ratio = (P₁ ÷ T₁) : (P₂ ÷ T₂).

questions.question: Simplify: x(2x - 8) + 5(x² -3) + 12
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Directly multiply the terms and combine them mentally.

For x² terms: x(2x) + 5(x²) = 2x² + 5x² = 7x²

For x terms: x(−8) = −8x

For constant terms: 5(−3) + 12 = −15 + 12 = −3

Combine all parts to get the final expression: 7x² − 8x − 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 7x² − 8x − 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x(2x − 8) + 5(x² − 3) + 12

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expand the first term using the distributive property:

⇒ x × 2x − x × 8 = 2x² − 8x

⇒ Expand the second term:

⇒ 5 × x² − 5 × 3 = 5x² − 15

⇒ Substitute these expanded forms back into the given expression:

⇒ (2x² − 8x) + (5x² − 15) + 12

⇒ Group the like terms together:

⇒ (2x² + 5x²) − 8x + (−15 + 12)

⇒ Add the coefficients of the grouped terms to simplify:

⇒ 7x² − 8x − 3

**∴ The correct answer is 7x² − 8x − 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Distributive Property

Multiplying a sum by a number is exactly the same as multiplying each addend by the number and then adding the products: a(b + c) = ab + ac.

Combining Like Terms

In algebraic simplification, terms with the same variables and powers are grouped, and their coefficients are added or subtracted together.

BODMAS Rule

This rule determines the correct order of operations in calculations: Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.
</p

Product of Two Numbers Rule

For any two positive integers, the product of the numbers is strictly equal to the product of their Highest Common Factor (HCF) and Least Common Multiple (LCM). This rule applies only to exactly two numbers, not three or more.

Co-prime Factors Property

questions.question: The number of prime numbers lying between 468 and 476, both included, is:

Between 468 and 476, ignore even numbers and multiples of 5.

Possible prime candidates are 469, 471, and 473.

469 = 7 × 67, 471 is divisible by 3 (sum of digits = 12), and 473 is divisible by 11 (4 − 7 + 3 = 0).

Since all candidates are composite, there are no prime numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

List the numbers and eliminate composite numbers using basic divisibility rules.

⇒ The numbers are: 468, 469, 470, 471, 472, 473, 474, 475, 476.

⇒ Eliminate all even numbers (divisible by 2): 468, 470, 472, 474, 476.

⇒ Eliminate numbers ending in 5 (divisible by 5): 475.

⇒ The remaining numbers to check are 469, 471, and 473.

⇒ For 469: It is divisible by 7 (469 = 7 × 67).

⇒ For 471: The sum of digits is 4 + 7 + 1 = 12. Since 12 is divisible by 3, 471 is divisible by 3.

⇒ For 473: The difference of alternate digits sum is (4 + 3) − 7 = 0. So, it is divisible by 11 (473 = 11 × 43).

⇒ Thus, none of the numbers between 468 and 476 are prime.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

Prime Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Checking Primality up to N

To check if a number N is prime, you only need to test divisibility by prime numbers up to √N.
